key_insight: Nano- and micro-textures in perovskite solar cells do more than reduce reflection: they also improve wetting, crystallinity, carrier extraction, and mechanical robustness.
engineering_relevance: Texture design is a practical device-engineering lever for boosting efficiency and reliability in perovskite photovoltaics, and may also benefit related optoelectronic devices.
method: Review of recent texture-related advances in perovskite solar cells
Focus on effects beyond light trapping: wetting, crystal quality, charge extraction, and flexibility
Synthesis of reported benefits across solar cells, photodetectors, and LEDs
evidence_signal: The paper is a literature review; the abstract reports qualitatively observed improvements across multiple texture-enabled studies rather than new experimental datasets.
watch_item: Benefits may depend strongly on the specific texture geometry, fabrication process, and perovskite deposition conditions, so not all texture strategies will generalize.
paper_title: More than just light management -- The multiple advantages of nano- and micro-textures in perovskite solar cells
